item.title: Trump admin blocks more than $1.6B in potentially improper Medicare lab payments, agency says
item.description: Dr. Mehmet Oz says labs billed Medicare for tests never performed as President Donald Trump's CMS uses AI to flag suspicious billing patterns.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Federal officials and the White House Task Force to Eliminate Fraud have blocked or clawed back more than $1.6 billion in potentially improper Medicare laboratory payments since President Donald Trump returned to office, including $732 million tied to 157 lab providers booted from the program for alleged fraud.

The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) said the labs were suspected of billing Medicare for tests that were never performed, tests patients did not need and services billed at higher rates than they should have been.

"When laboratories bill Medicare for tests they never performed, it drains the Medicare Trust Fund and diverts resources away from beneficiaries who need them," CMS Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz said.

DOJ CHARGES 19 DEFENDANTS IN ALLEGED $4M PHILADELPHIA MEDICARE AND MEDICAID FRAUD

In one case, the owner of a consulting company enrolled 14 labs in Medicare and billed the program more than $24 million, even though CMS said none of the labs appeared to be operating.

CMS has since held back $12 million in payments to the labs and recovered another $7 million. Eleven of the 14 labs have been removed from Medicare, while the remaining three are still under investigation.

CMS said it is using artificial intelligence and other technology to sift through Medicare claims and spot unusual billing that could be a sign of fraud.

The technology looks for billing that falls outside normal patterns and can flag suspicious claims for closer scrutiny. CMS can then hold, reject or deny a claim before Medicare pays it.

Of the $1.6 billion cited by the agency, more than $500 million in suspected fraudulent payments were stopped through 185 payment suspensions after CMS investigated 600 labs.

"The previous administration treated our taxpayer-funded programs as piggy banks for fraudsters," the White House told Fox News Digital. "That is no longer the case, thanks to President Donald Trump, Vice President JD Vance, and Dr. Oz, who is an anti-fraud superstar."

TREASURY HAILS SUCCESS OF ANTI-FRAUD PROCESS THAT FLAGGED AND PREVENTED $99 MILLION IN PAYMENTS TO DEAD PEOPLE

The agency also recovered more than $276 million in overpayments made to 442 suspect labs and said another $127 million in potentially fraudulent payments was prevented after 85 cases were referred to law enforcement.

CMS pointed to two recent cases in Texas as examples of labs suspected of billing Medicare for services they did not provide.

One lab began billing Medicare in late February. CMS said it caught the suspicious activity early and denied $1.2 million in claims.

The lab then changed the way it billed Medicare in early April in an apparent attempt to get around the agency’s safeguards, according to CMS. Officials continued watching its claims and stopped more than $150,000 in additional payments before removing the provider from Medicare later that month.

DR OZ SAYS 800 HOSPICE PROVIDERS SUSPENDED IN CALIFORNIA OVER ALLEGED $1B MEDICARE FRAUD SCHEME

Another Texas lab began billing heavily in May after submitting test claims two days earlier in the year. CMS denied $1.9 million in claims and captured another $1.7 million in payments. The lab remains under review and could be removed from Medicare.

The lab cases are part of a wider Trump administration push to combat improper Medicare billing involving medical equipment, hospice care, skin treatments and other services.

CMS said its Medicare fraud prevention efforts saved $42 billion in fiscal year 2025. So far in 2026, the agency says it has identified $1.8 billion in Medicare overpayments and recovered $378 million in overpayments from post-payment reviews.

Since Jan. 1, CMS has also frozen more than $371 million in Medicare payments involving 267 providers and suppliers. That includes more than $226 million in suspected improper billing for medical equipment, more than $53 million involving skin treatments and more than $23 million involving hospice providers.

"We won't stop until we've restored program integrity and ensured that fraudsters have nowhere left to hide," Oz said.

item.title: ICE officer charged in Minneapolis shooting released in Texas after judge declines to intervene
item.description: Christian Castro, an ICE officer charged in connection with a shooting in Minnesota, was released from lock up in Texas after a judge declined a temporary restraining order.
item.content:encoded:
A U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer who was charged in connection with shooting someone in Minnesota earlier this year was released from lockup in Texas on Thursday.

A judge on Wednesday declined to take action to prevent the man's release and force Texas Gov. Greg Abbott to send the individual back to Minnesota. Minnesota officials have been pushing to have the man held as they fight for his extradition in the Hennepin County case.

The man, Christian Castro, "was released at 6:59 a.m.," Cameron County Sheriff Manuel Trevino told Fox News Digital in an email on Thursday.

Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty announced in May that Castro was "being charged with four counts of assault in the second degree and one count of falsely reporting a crime."

JUDGE CLEARS PATH FOR ICE AGENT ACCUSED IN MINNESOTA SHOOTING CASE TO LEAVE TEXAS JAIL

"Mr. Castro fired his service weapon at the front door of a home knowing there were people who had just run inside that presented absolutely no harm to him or anyone else," Moriarty asserted, saying the bullet hit Julio Sosa-Celis in the leg and eventually lodged "in the wall of a child's bedroom."

Castro was arrested in Texas, and Minnesota has been pressing for Texas to extradite him from the Lone Star State.

'POLITICAL STUNT' PROSECUTION OF ICE AGENT FOR 'ROAD RAGE' PROVOKES HEATED DHS RESPONSE

U.S. District Judge Fernando Rodriguez, Jr.'s Wednesday order denying a temporary restraining order declared, "In May, the State of Minnesota charged Castro with various crimes based on that incident. By the time these charges arose, however, Castro was no longer in Minnesota, leading a county judge to issue a nationwide warrant for his arrest. When authorities in the State of Texas arrested Castro in late May, Minnesota Governor Tim Walz initiated the process under the Extradition Act of 1793 and the Uniform Criminal Extradition Act to secure Castro’s extradition to Minnesota."

"Under the UCEA, Castro can be detained on the strength of the Minnesota warrant only until August 27, 2026. As the day approached, and fearing that Castro will flee into Mexico should he be released, Minnesota made repeated inquiries of Texas regarding the status of the extradition request. On August 18, having not received a definitive answer, Minnesota filed this action, alleging that Governor Abbott 'has refused' to sign a rendition warrant, violating the Extradition Clause of the United States Constitution, the Extradition Act, and the UCEA," the order stated.

ABBOTT TAUNTS FAR-LEFT AG WITH FIERY WARNING OVER ICE EXTRADITION FIGHT: 'SUCH BAD LAWYERS'

"Minnesota moves for a temporary restraining order to avoid Castro’s release before Governor Abbott signs a rendition warrant. On August 25, the Court held a hearing on the request. Based on the record and the applicable law, the Court concludes that Minnesota fails to satisfy the requirements for the issuance of a temporary restraining order," the judge's order noted.

item.title: Man accused of posing as 49ers player in $1.3M romance scam appeared in video obtained by OutKick
item.description: An FBI affidavit details how Daejon Labrayae Love allegedly used a fake 49ers persona, custom helmets and prop money to defraud 26 women of $1.3M.
item.content:encoded:
OutKick obtained a video in late 2024 that appears to show Daejon Labrayae Love signing what he represented to be an NFL contract.

When the cameraman asks Love who he is signing with, Love responds, "Niners, you already know, Niner gang."

OutKick did not publish a story at the time because we could not independently verify Love’s claimed NFL affiliation and had no evidence that he had sought or received money from women.

The material suggested Love was using a purported 49ers affiliation to impress women but didn't indicate an investment scheme.

MORE DETAILS ABOUT JED YORK'S ARREST IN A PROSTITUTION STING COME TO LIGHT AND BEGS QUESTIONS ABOUT THE 49ERS

Now, newly unsealed federal court records provide a far different account.

An FBI affidavit says Love filmed himself "supposedly signing an employment contract with the 49ers" while claiming he would be a wide receiver for the team. The video obtained by OutKick appears to match the affidavit’s description.

Representatives for the NFL and 49ers told investigators Love had never been employed by the team or the league, according to the affidavit.

On Aug. 25, 2026, the Justice Department announced that Love, 35, and Taylor Jamie Chan, 18, were charged in Portland, Oregon, with conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud.

Federal authorities allege Love and Chan used a false 49ers persona, a lavish lifestyle, fictitious investment accounts and romantic relationships to defraud 26 women in Oregon, Washington, Idaho and California out of about $1.3 million.

The affidavit says Love allegedly portrayed himself to women as an NFL player for the 49ers or a wealthy Swiss real estate developer. Chan allegedly posed as Love’s financial advisor, joining three-way FaceTime calls with women and displaying purported investment gains.

Investigators said Love posted misleading photographs, videos and statements online to support the 49ers claim.

FORMER COLLEGE BASKETBALL GUARD KERR KRIISA INDICTED IN ALLEGED $2.2M WIRE FRAUD SCHEME

The FBI also said Love posted screen-recorded videos that appeared to show legitimate NFL players, with the original posters’ information removed. According to the affidavit, Love then presented the videos as his own to convince women he played for the 49ers.

Agents identified three videos from Love’s iCloud accounts that had been shared roughly 185 times, including with numerous alleged victims. Two showed Love wearing a 49ers jacket, according to the affidavit.

In one video, Love allegedly said San Francisco "offered me the most money," claimed he had received a signing bonus and said he attended team meetings and workouts.

The affidavit says Love also claimed friendships with current and former NFL players Tyreek Hill, Antonio Brown and John Brown, and used those purported relationships to explain how he received tryout invitations.

Investigators said Love’s financial records showed no identifiable legitimate income and no direct deposits or payroll checks from the 49ers or another legitimate employer.

Court records also describe how investigators say Love built his image online and in person.

The FBI said Love spent more than $1,160 at Green Gridiron, a website that sells custom football helmets. Investigators also found purchases from Prop Money Inc., which sells realistic fake cash for movies, and from companies that sell social media followers, likes and views.

Love posted photos in 49ers apparel and was photographed with a 49ers helmet. He also had a 49ers-themed "LOVE 1" cake.

The affidavit alleges Love used phone applications to create fake bank and investment account balances that he then showed women as proof of his wealth and investment success.

In January 2024, according to the affidavit, Love asked Chan to make a screenshot showing a $3.4 million account balance. The following month, investigators say Love asked Chan to create a stock account appearing to be worth $11 million.

SHE DIDN’T EXIST, BUT THE MONEY DID: A REAL INFLUENCER SOUNDS THE ALARM ON AI DECEPTION

The government alleges Chan helped give the alleged scheme credibility by posing as Love’s financial advisor. Chan allegedly exchanged messages with Love about fictitious investment opportunities, then joined FaceTime calls in which women were shown false investment gains.

Love and Chan were arrested together at Boise Airport on Aug. 24, 2026, according to the Justice Department.

The complaint lists an alleged offense window of February 2022 through March 2026, while the Justice Department said the alleged scheme continued until the Aug. 24 arrests.

The affidavit identifies Chan as 18 but does not list his date of birth. Under the government’s timeline, Chan would have been 13 or 14 when the alleged scheme began. In the affidavit’s first detailed account from February 2022, Love allegedly told a woman within days of meeting her on a dating app to invest $10,000 with Chan.

In a separate Idaho filing, prosecutors asked a judge to detain Love pending his transfer to Oregon. The government alleged Love was wearing 49ers apparel when he was arrested and that agents later found $3,000 in cash and 49ers gear, including a helmet, in an Airbnb associated with him.

As of publication, OutKick could not immediately verify whether detention or transfer rulings had been entered following their scheduled initial appearances.

Prosecutors also said in their Idaho detention motion that Love was in Boise while actively trying to defraud three additional Idaho victims.

The San Francisco 49ers and Love’s attorney did not respond to requests for comment before publication.

Love and Chan are presumed innocent unless and until proven guilty.

item.title: House Dem's 'Lake Natalie' jab at Trump aide sets social media ablaze: 'Stay classy'
item.description: House Democrat Debbie Dingell's quip about renaming Lake Ontario "Lake Natalie" after a Trump aide sparked fierce backlash and left-wing praise.
item.content:encoded:
A House Democrat's jab at one of President Donald Trump's most loyal aides prompted a firestorm on social media.

Rep. Debbie Dingell, D-Mich., is getting heat from the right and praise from the left after she quipped about Trump's decision to rename Lake Ontario. 

"Let’s just call it Lake Natalie so we know you’ll start protecting our Great Lakes," she wrote on X.

Trump signed an order on Thursday renaming one of the five Great Lakes "Lake America" amid an ongoing trade dispute with Canada.

HOUSE DEM DEBBIE DINGELL PLACES TRUMP'S LAKE ONTARIO NAME CHANGE IN THE CROSSHAIRS

Dingell's comment appears to be aimed at Trump aide Natalie Harp, a close confidante of the president, whom Democrats have seized on after she was reportedly one of the small group of people who joined Trump on a separate plane after a potential Iranian plot to take down Air Force One.

The comment has prompted fierce backlash from Trump allies who accuse Democrats of unfairly targeting a White House aide trying to do her job — a sentiment that was on full display online this week.

JON OSSOFF DODGES ON WHY HE INVOKED TRUMP AIDE'S NAME DURING GEORGIA CAMPAIGN RALLY

"You're being exactly who I said Democrats were all along. You don't care about protecting women from sexism/misogyny. You just care if they have an R behind their name," GOP commentator Melik Abdul wrote on X.

Retired Air Force Lt. Col. Robert "Buzz" Patterson said, "Wow. Stay classy, Michigan."

OBAMA STRATEGIST TURNS ON RISING DEM STAR OVER VIRAL TRUMP ATTACK: 'GRATUITOUS AND UNNECESSARY'

"Ouch! Not so nice to a young woman staffer .. i suspect your target is the President but it is not nice to the young staffer.. why does she deserve this ? …this all started with a snarky comment by a dem senator," veteran news anchor Greta Van Susteren wrote.

Van Susteren was referencing a comment by Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., that kicked off the frenzy over Harp in the first place. Ossoff said during a rally that Trump would rather "build his ballroom and travel with Natalie" than do the job of president.

CNN, MS NOW HAVE MENTIONED TRUMP AIDE NATALIE HARP HUNDREDS OF TIMES SINCE OSSOFF'S VIRAL JAB

"Is this the new move when a dem wants to pretend they’re relevant?" former Trump spokeswoman Elizabeth Pipko wrote on X.

But left-wing social media circles cheered Dingell on.

"Debbie wins the Internet today, full stop," wrote former conservative lawyer and failed congressional candidate George Conway.

Democrat Janice Hough wrote, "Rep. Debbie, I was not familiar with your game."

"Debbie hits a grand slam," quipped Norman Ornstein, contributing editor for The Atlantic.

item.title: Biden-honored Iraqi official lands on US terror watchlist as Trump State Dept revokes visa
item.description: Taif Sami Mohammed received the International Women of Courage Award in 2022 but now appears on the U.S. terrorist watchlist with her visa revoked.
item.content:encoded:
FIRST ON FOX: Four years ago, Taif Sami Mohammed was being celebrated by the United States as one of the world’s most courageous women. Secretary of State Antony Blinken praised the senior Iraqi official as the country’s "Iron Woman," crediting her with stopping bribes, uncovering schemes that enriched corrupt officials and fighting corruption despite threats against her.

Today, Mohammed is believed to be outside Iraq, on the U.S. terrorist watchlist and can no longer enter the United States.

A State Department official told Fox News Digital that the department revoked Mohammed’s visa this week, marking a dramatic reversal for an official who received one of the Biden administration’s highest-profile awards for women in 2022.

"While the Biden State Department shamefully celebrated and awarded foreigners who threaten our nation, the Trump State Department revokes their visas and ensures these individuals are removed from our country," Assistant Secretary of State for Global Public Affairs Dylan Johnson told Fox News Digital.

TRUMP ADMIN EYES HISTORIC MASS VISA REVOCATION TARGETING UP TO 200K ASYLUM SEEKERS: REPORT

"Under President Trump and Secretary Rubio, suspected terrorists will never be allowed to remain in the United States."

The State Department did not immediately provide details about when Mohammed was placed on the terrorist watchlist or the intelligence that led to that determination.

Mohammed’s fall from Washington’s favor had been building publicly for more than a year.

Republican lawmakers previously accused her of helping facilitate terrorist financing through Iraq’s financial system and urged the Trump administration to take action against her. Reps. Joe Wilson, R-S.C., and Greg Steube, R-Fla., called Mohammed a "key enabler of terrorist funding in Iraq" and pushed the administration to impose sanctions.

Those allegations stand in stark contrast to how the Biden administration described Mohammed when it selected her for the State Department’s International Women of Courage Award in 2022.

At the time, Mohammed was Iraq’s deputy finance minister and director general of its budget department. The State Department described her as a "frontline leader against corrupt practices" who had been integral to preventing corruption in Iraq’s budget.

Blinken went further during the March 2022 awards ceremony, saying Mohammed had "stopped bribes" and uncovered efforts to inflate government payrolls and enrich corrupt officials.

The ceremony, hosted by Blinken and featuring remarks from then-first lady Jill Biden, honored twelve women whom the State Department said had shown extraordinary courage and leadership.

Mohammed later rose to become Iraq’s finance minister, overseeing the federal budget, government spending and Baghdad’s financial relationship with Iraq’s Kurdistan region.

Her troubles have since spread beyond Washington.

An Iraqi court summoned Mohammed and placed her on a judicial wanted list as authorities widened a corruption investigation into former senior government officials, IraqiNews reported Aug. 9, 2025, citing sources familiar with the proceedings.

FBI BRINGS IRAQI MAN ACCUSED OF COORDINATING NEARLY 20 TERROR ATTACKS IN EUROPE TO FACE TRIAL IN NEW YORK

According to the report, Mohammed is believed to be outside Iraq and has not been detained. The court action is part of an investigation and does not establish that she committed wrongdoing.

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

The investigation grew out of a broader corruption probe involving government contracts and large sums of public money and has reached other former Iraqi officials, according to the report.

Mohammed’s placement on the U.S. terrorist watchlist represents a separate and potentially more serious development. The State Department has not said whether it is connected to the terrorist financing allegations raised by members of Congress, the Iraqi corruption investigation or other intelligence gathered by the U.S. government.

item.title: Country singer Lauren Alaina credits small-town Georgia roots for strong work ethic, faith
item.description: Lauren Alaina reveals how growing up in Rossville, Georgia shaped her faith and work ethic ahead of her deeply personal fourth album, "Stages."
item.content:encoded:
Country singer Lauren Alaina is thankful for her small town roots and the lessons they taught her.

During a recent interview with Fox News Digital, the 31-year-old singer spoke about her upcoming album, "Stages," and shared why she credits growing up in Rossville, Georgia for her success and her work ethic.

"I come from a long line of hardworking people and believers and dreamers in their own way, whatever their path was," she said. "Mine obviously looked very different than the rest of my family because my working hard and my dreaming was leaving home and going to a new place, which people don't do a ton in Rossville, Georgia."

She explained that not only did she learn the importance of working hard from growing up in her small town, but also of "being kind, being grateful [and] being funny," saying she got her "sense of humor from back home for sure."

One of "the biggest lessons" she learned, growing up in her small town, is to keep "working hard and being kind to people, and if you work hard, it pays off."

WATCH: Lauren Alaina credits her small town upbringing for her work ethic and faith

"I do think my work ethic definitely came from watching every one of my family. My mom worked really hard, my dad worked really hard, and my grandparents. They all had very different careers and different lives, but they just worked really hard and they kept their faith strong."

As an adult, she is now "thankful" to have grown up where she did and to have a strong faith and work ethic as some of the things were instilled in her throughout her upbringing.

Alaina is gearing up for the release of her fourth studio album, "Stages," which she calls "a deeply personal album," which covers three different phases of her life.

"It feels like it represents me fully because I feel like I finally landed in the place of who I am supposed to be in this stage of my life," she said. "And I was able to kind of take a look back and share all of my stories. I'm really proud of it. It's a deeply personal album. It's really fun too. It's not overly serious. It is serious in parts and carefree and my mid 20s in parts and represents my hometown in parts as well. So I'm very proud of that."

The "Road Less Traveled" singer admits that each stage was hard for her to revisit, be it her parents' divorce, navigating heartbreak and losing her father unexpectedly.

WATCH: Lauren Alaina titled her latest album 'Stages' to represent the different phases of her life

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR THE ENTERTAINMENT NEWSLETTER

There are bright spots in there too, including when she met her husband and when she welcomed her daughter.

"I closed the album with a song called 'Heaven Sent,' which is one of my favorites, and it's about my dad sending my daughter for me to help me heal and move forward," she said. item.description: Danica McKellar reveals Dolly Parton slept only three to five hours a night and did her own hair and makeup before arriving on set each morning.
item.content:encoded:
Dolly Parton's former co-star, Danica McKellar, is sharing who the country music legend really was when the cameras weren't rolling.

During an interview with Fox News Digital, McKellar said that Parton told her that she would only sleep three to five hours a night and then wake up and do her own hair and make-up.

"She told me she only slept three to five hours a night. She was always dreaming stuff up and just busy. She'd sleep on her big travel bus, if she was traveling and doing things, and wake up early in the morning... She did her own hair and makeup, her own wig and her own makeup. And she'd get to work," McKellar said.

McKellar's professional relationship with Parton began through Parton's Imagination Library, which included McKellar’s children’s book, "Goodnight, Numbers," in its literacy program.

McKellar later narrated the documentary "The Library That Dolly Built" before pitching the idea for the 2019 Hallmark movie "Christmas at Dollywood," in which she starred opposite Parton.

While working with Parton, McKellar told Fox News Digital that the "9 to 5" singer was "everything that you hope she could possibly be and much more."

"She's incredible, great work ethic. She wanted to rehearse a lot and I was like, 'I would love to rehearse with you.' I'd love to just be in her presence. She was incredible. She walked on the set and made everyone feel comfortable because people were so nervous to meet Dolly Parton."

item.title: Hillary Clinton's dig at Trump over Lake Ontario name change sparks viral backlash: 'Shooting blanks'
item.description: Hillary Clinton's post defending the Lake Ontario name sparked immediate conservative backlash, with her failed presidential run becoming the target.
item.content:encoded:
Former secretary of state and Democratic presidential candidate Hillary Clinton found herself on the wrong end of social media criticism after taking issue with President Donald Trump’s move to rename Lake Ontario amid a heated trade war with Canada.

"It's Lake Ontario," Clinton posted on Thursday, inserting herself into the debate stemming from Trump’s executive order instructing the Department of Interior to refer to the lake as "Lake America" from now on.

Clinton, whose X account does not allow replies, was immediately mocked by conservatives over her failed presidential run against Trump as the post surpassed 3 million views in just a few hours.

"It’s not President Hillary Clinton…and never will be," conservative commentator CJ Pearson posted on X.

CLINTON’S EYEBROW-RAISING SOCIALISM TAKE SPARKS BRUTAL MOCKERY: ‘DEFINITION OF INSANITY’

"Trump Controls the News Cycle Volume 87187585124782," former Trump DHS Assistant Secretary for Public Affairs Tricia McLaughlin posted on X.

"It’s President Donald J. Trump," the Republican National Committee (RNC) posted on X.

"And you’ll never be President," Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., posted on X.

‘CAPTAIN CANADA’ FIREBRAND UNLOADS ON TRUMP WITH PROFANE ONE-LINER AS TRADE WAR ESCALATES

"Loser says what?" conservative commentator Jillian King Anderson posted on X.

"Democrats preferring Canada to America is the least surprising thing I’ve seen all day," conservative commentator Michael Knowles posted on X.

"Hillary's out here shooting blanks ," conservative radio host Vince Coglianese posted on X.

Trump's move to rename the lake, which sits on the U.S.-Canada border, came amid a breakdown in trade between both nations, with Trump accusing Ottawa of unfair trade practices.

The U.S. imposed new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods such as wine, furniture and dairy products, while Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said U.S. trade demands proved Washington wanted to "destroy our major industries," including autos, steel and aluminum.

"Canada has been ripping us off for a long time on trade," Trump said Thursday. "Very sadly, even the military, you know, we defend Canada for nothing. We don't get anything. They don't pay us to defend Canada."

Trump previously used geographic names to make political statements, ordering the renaming of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America in January 2025.

"The Lake of America was something I've been thinking about for a long time, actually. As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico — we changed it — and now it's very routinely the Gulf of America," Trump said in the Oval Office on Thursday.

Several prominent Democrats have come out against the name change, including New York's Democratic Gov. Kathy Hochul who said New York, which borders the lake's southern side, "won't be calling it that."

Fox News Digital's Louis Casiano contributed to this report
